accepted.s: Which one of the following best describes the inland fisheries strategy adopted in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Fish seed stocking combined with reservoir and tank fisheries
Replacement of freshwater fisheries with marine aquaculture
Conversion of all departmental tanks into industrial zones
accepted.x: The inland fisheries strategy includes fish seed stocking and the development of reservoir and tank fisheries. Departmental tanks are leased to fishermen cooperative societies.
accepted.tq: Identify the operational components of the strategy rather than a broad sectoral label.
accepted.sec: Inland fisheries - reservoir, tank, brackish-water aquaculture; leading districts

accepted.s: Departmental tanks in Andhra Pradesh are leased primarily to which of the following?
accepted.x: Departmental tanks are leased to fishermen cooperative societies for fisheries development.
accepted.tq: Test the institutional responsibility through a nearby-organisation trap.
accepted.sec: Inland fisheries - reservoir, tank, brackish-water aquaculture; leading districts

accepted.s: The registered aquaculture area in Andhra Pradesh is approximately:
accepted.x: The registered aquaculture area in Andhra Pradesh is 2.89 lakh acres.
accepted.tq: Distinguish closely spaced numerical values.
accepted.sec: Inland fisheries - reservoir, tank, brackish-water aquaculture; leading districts

accepted.s:
With reference to the geo-tagging of aquaculture ponds in Andhra Pradesh, consider the following statements:
1. 2,07,765 ponds have been mapped.
2. The mapped area is 5,79,697 acres.
3. The ponds have been organised into 3,725 clusters and 69 mega clusters.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: 2,07,765 ponds covering 5,79,697 acres were mapped into 3,725 clusters and 69 mega clusters.
accepted.tq: Combine a numerical set and verify each statement independently.
accepted.sec: Inland fisheries - reservoir, tank, brackish-water aquaculture; leading districts

accepted.s: Which one of the following is a freshwater alternative species promoted in Andhra Pradesh aquaculture?
accepted.x: GIFT tilapia is listed among the freshwater alternative species. Cobia, lobster and mussel are brackish-water or marine alternatives.
accepted.tq: Separate freshwater species from brackish-water alternatives.
accepted.sec: Inland fisheries - reservoir, tank, brackish-water aquaculture; leading districts

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Groupers are listed as brackish-water alternatives, not freshwater species. P. indicus and sea bass are brackish-water species, while Jayanti rohu is a freshwater species.
accepted.tq: Find the reversed classification in a closely related list.
accepted.sec: Inland fisheries - reservoir, tank, brackish-water aquaculture; leading districts

accepted.s: Which one of the following districts is NOT included among the leading aquaculture districts of Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: The leading aquaculture districts listed are West Godavari, Eluru, Krishna, Bapatla, Nellore, Konaseema and Kakinada. Anakapalli is not included in that list.
accepted.tq: Use elimination from the exact district list.
accepted.sec: Inland fisheries - reservoir, tank, brackish-water aquaculture; leading districts

accepted.s: Which group of districts is identified as the shrimp backbone of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Prakasam, West Godavari, East Godavari, Nellore and Krishna
Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, Anakapalli and Bapatla
Guntur, Anantapur, Kurnool, Nellore and Srikakulam
Eluru, Kakinada, Konaseema, Kadapa and Chittoor
accepted.x: The shrimp backbone comprises Prakasam, West Godavari, East Godavari, Nellore and Krishna districts.
accepted.tq: Recall a named regional grouping without substituting neighbouring coastal districts.
accepted.sec: Inland fisheries - reservoir, tank, brackish-water aquaculture; leading districts

accepted.s: In 2025–26, West Godavari produced approximately how much fish and shrimp, valued at about what amount?
accepted.x: West Godavari produced 9.64 lakh metric tonnes of fish and shrimp worth ₹24,345 crore in 2025–26.
accepted.tq: Match the production figure with its corresponding value.
accepted.sec: Inland fisheries - reservoir, tank, brackish-water aquaculture; leading districts

accepted.s: The Integrated Aqua Park at Parasavaripalem is located in which district and is being developed under which scheme?
o: Nellore district under the Blue Revolution Mission
Kakinada district under the Coastal Aquaculture Authority
accepted.x: The Integrated Aqua Park at Parasavaripalem in Bapatla district is being developed under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY). Its approved cost is ₹88.08 crore.
accepted.tq: Link place, district and implementing scheme.
accepted.sec: Inland fisheries - reservoir, tank, brackish-water aquaculture; leading districts

accepted.s: How many integrated aqua laboratories are planned in Andhra Pradesh, and how many are working?
accepted.x: Thirty-five integrated aqua laboratories are planned, of which 30 are working.
accepted.tq: Avoid reversing planned and operational numbers.
accepted.sec: Inland fisheries - reservoir, tank, brackish-water aquaculture; leading districts

accepted.s: In India, inland fisheries contribute more than what proportion of total fish output?
accepted.x: Inland fisheries contribute more than 75 percent of India’s total fish output.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct threshold rather than an approximate lower share.
accepted.sec: Inland fisheries - reservoir, tank, brackish-water aquaculture; leading districts

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:

List-I (Fishing harbour)
 a. Juvvaladinne
 b. Uppada
 c. Nizampatnam
 d. Machilipatnam

List-II (District)

accepted.s: Which fishing harbour had achieved the highest progress among the Phase I harbours as of October 2025?
accepted.x: Juvvaladinne had the highest reported progress at 97.98 percent, followed by Uppada at 84.29 percent, Nizampatnam at 81.61 percent and Machilipatnam at 71.45 percent.
accepted.tq: Compare the numerical progress figures rather than the district names.
accepted.sec: Marine fisheries - fishing harbours and fish landing centres → district

accepted.s:
Arrange the Phase I fishing harbours in descending order of reported progress as of October 2025:
A. Uppada
B. Machilipatnam
C. Juvvaladinne
D. Nizampatnam
accepted.x: The descending order is Juvvaladinne (97.98%), Uppada (84.29%), Nizampatnam (81.61%) and Machilipatnam (71.45%).
accepted.tq: Order the options by their stated numerical values.
accepted.sec: Marine fisheries - fishing harbours and fish landing centres → district

accepted.s: The total cost of Phase I fishing harbour works in Andhra Pradesh, according to the 2025–26 survey, is:
accepted.x: The Phase I fishing harbour works were estimated at ₹1,522.80 crore in the 2025–26 survey. The earlier agreement in March 2021 was for ₹1,204.56 crore.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the revised project cost from the earlier agreement value.
accepted.sec: Marine fisheries - fishing harbours and fish landing centres → district

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the Phase II fishing harbour projects in Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: Phase II includes Biyyaputhippa, Kothapatnam, Pudimadaka, Budagatlapalem and Vodarevu. Machilipatnam belongs to the Phase I list.
accepted.tq: Separate Phase I and Phase II through the project-stage trap.
accepted.sec: Marine fisheries - fishing harbours and fish landing centres → district

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with a Phase II fishing harbour?
accepted.x: Biyyaputhippa is in West Godavari. Kothapatnam is in Prakasam, Pudimadaka in Anakapalli and Budagatlapalem in Srikakulam.
accepted.tq: Check the district against the project name and reject swapped locations.
accepted.sec: Marine fisheries - fishing harbours and fish landing centres → district

accepted.s: The modernisation of Visakhapatnam Fishing Harbour and the upgrading of Kakinada Fishing Harbour are being undertaken under:
o: The WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies
accepted.x: The upgrades are under PMMSY, not Sagarmala. Visakhapatnam Fishing Harbour modernisation costs ₹178.51 crore and Kakinada Fishing Harbour works cost ₹58.95 crore.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between two neighbouring coastal development programmes.
accepted.sec: Marine fisheries - fishing harbours and fish landing centres → district

accepted.s: The ICAR-CMFRI Regional Centre at Visakhapatnam is located at Lawsons Bay Colony and is associated with:
accepted.x: The ICAR-CMFRI Regional Centre at Lawsons Bay Colony, Visakhapatnam, is associated with open-sea cage farming.
accepted.tq: Match an institution with its specialised activity.
accepted.sec: Fisheries institutions in AP → location

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: AP Fisheries University — Lawsons Bay Colony, Visakhapatnam
MPEDA brood multiplication centre — West Godavari
accepted.x: The ICAR-CIFT Research Centre is located at Pandurangapuram, Visakhapatnam. The AP Fisheries University is in West Godavari, the MPEDA centre is in Visakhapatnam, and the ICAR-CMFRI regional centre is at Lawsons Bay Colony.
accepted.tq: Use location-based elimination among fisheries institutions.
accepted.sec: Fisheries institutions in AP → location

accepted.s: The AP Fisheries University was established under which Act and is located in which district?
o: AP Fisheries University Act, 2020 — West Godavari
accepted.x: The AP Fisheries University was established under the AP Fisheries University Act, 2020, and is located in West Godavari district.
accepted.tq: Combine the enabling law with the institutional location.
accepted.sec: Fisheries institutions in AP → location

accepted.s: The brood multiplication centre of MPEDA at Visakhapatnam is associated with which species?
accepted.x: The MPEDA Rajiv Gandhi Centre for Aquaculture brood multiplication centre at Visakhapatnam is associated with P. monodon.
accepted.tq: Distinguish two similar shrimp species by their institutional association.
accepted.sec: Fisheries institutions in AP → location

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding fisheries institutions:
1. MPEDA is a statutory body under the Ministry of Commerce.
2. The headquarters of MPEDA is at Kochi.
3. The ICAR-CIFT Research Centre in Andhra Pradesh is located at Kakinada.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false: the ICAR-CIFT Research Centre is at Pandurangapuram, Visakhapatnam.
accepted.tq: Reject the swapped-location statement after confirming the statutory status.
accepted.sec: Fisheries institutions in AP → location

accepted.s: Land situated within 2 km of the High Tide Line is regulated by which authority under the Coastal Aquaculture Authority Act and Rules?
o: Coastal Aquaculture Authority of the Government of India
Andhra Pradesh State Aquaculture Development Authority
accepted.x: Land within 2 km of the High Tide Line is regulated by the Coastal Aquaculture Authority of the Government of India under the CAA Act and Rules, 2005, amended in 2023.
accepted.tq: Ask which authority would legally exercise the power.
accepted.sec: AP aquaculture regulation - APSADA Act 2020, zones

accepted.s: Freshwater farms in Andhra Pradesh are licensed by APSADA through which portal?
accepted.x: Freshwater farms are licensed by APSADA through the e-Matsyakar portal.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact official portal name and avoid look-alike labels.
accepted.sec: AP aquaculture regulation - APSADA Act 2020, zones

accepted.s: Which of the following Acts was NOT included among the Andhra Pradesh aquaculture-related Acts of 2020?
accepted.x: The 2020 group included the APSADA Act, AP Fish Feed (Quality Control) Act, AP Aquaculture Seed (Quality Control) (Amendment) Act and AP Fisheries University Act. The AP Marine Fishing Regulation Act dates from 1995.
accepted.tq: Use the year trap to distinguish the 2020 Acts from the 1995 regulation law.
accepted.sec: AP aquaculture regulation - APSADA Act 2020, zones

accepted.s: The notified aqua zones in Andhra Pradesh are primarily relevant for determining eligibility for:
o: The ₹88.08 crore aqua park grant only
accepted.x: Notified aqua zones determine eligibility for the ₹1.50 tariff. The other options relate to different fisheries provisions.
accepted.tq: Link the regulatory zone with its specific economic benefit.
accepted.sec: AP aquaculture regulation - APSADA Act 2020, zones

accepted.s: The uniform marine fishing ban on India’s East Coast is observed for how many days and during which period?
accepted.x: The uniform ban is for 61 days, from 15 April to 14 June on the East Coast. In 2026, it was specified as midnight of 15 April to midnight of 14 June.
accepted.tq: Separate the exact duration and dates from plausible altered periods.
accepted.sec: Fishing-ban period and marine fishing regulation

accepted.s: During the fishing-ban period in Andhra Pradesh, which craft are exempt from the ban?
o: Motorised boats operating within 12 nautical miles
accepted.x: Traditional non-motorised craft are exempt. Mechanised and motorised boats are banned in territorial waters during the specified period.
accepted.tq: Apply the exemption clause to the boat category described.
accepted.sec: Fishing-ban period and marine fishing regulation

accepted.s: Penalties for violation of the Andhra Pradesh fishing-ban provisions are imposed under the:
accepted.x: Penalties for the relevant fishing-ban violations are imposed under the AP Marine Fishing Regulation Act, 1995.
accepted.tq: Match the enforcement provision with the correct statute and year.
accepted.sec: Fishing-ban period and marine fishing regulation

accepted.s: The territorial waters referred to in Andhra Pradesh’s proposed action against IUU fishing extend up to:
accepted.x: The proposal concerns IUU fishing in Andhra Pradesh’s territorial waters, extending up to 12 nautical miles.
accepted.tq: Distinguish territorial waters from the wider exclusive economic zone.
accepted.sec: Fishing-ban period and marine fishing regulation

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes India’s position regarding the WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies?
o: India accepted it as the 123rd member, and aquaculture and inland fishing are exempt.
India rejected it at MC12, and only marine fishing is exempt.
India accepted it as the 23rd member, and inland fishing is prohibited.
India accepted it in 2022, and all fisheries subsidies are exempt.
accepted.x: The Agreement was adopted at MC12 in 2022 and entered into force in September 2025. India became the 123rd member to accept it, while aquaculture and inland fishing are exempt.
accepted.tq: Test membership number, effective date and exemption scope together.
accepted.sec: Fishing-ban period and marine fishing regulation

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about Kolleru Lake is correct?
1. It is the largest freshwater lake in Andhra Pradesh.
2. It covers approximately 305 square kilometres according to the cited current figure.
3. It is fed by the Tammileru among other streams.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Kolleru is Andhra Pradesh’s largest freshwater lake, has a current cited area of about 305 sq km, and receives water from the Tammileru among other sources.
accepted.tq: Verify a location, size and drainage fact as a single factual cluster.
accepted.sec: Kolleru lake aquaculture - encroachment issue

accepted.s: Kolleru Wildlife Sanctuary is associated with which of the following bird species as a breeding ground?
accepted.x: Kolleru Wildlife Sanctuary is a breeding ground of the spot-billed pelican and also supports painted storks.
accepted.tq: Identify the characteristic wildlife association of the wetland.
accepted.sec: Kolleru lake aquaculture - encroachment issue

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the protection status of Kolleru is correct?
o: The sanctuary limit is the −5 ft contour and it became a Ramsar site in 1992.
The sanctuary limit is the +5 ft contour and it has been a Ramsar site since 2002.
The sanctuary limit is the +10 ft contour and it became a Ramsar site in 2010.
The sanctuary limit is the sea-level contour and it has no Ramsar status.
accepted.x: The sanctuary boundary is defined by the +5 ft contour, and Kolleru has been a Ramsar site since 2002.
accepted.tq: Combine two statutory and date-based identifiers without reversing the figures.
accepted.sec: Kolleru lake aquaculture - encroachment issue

accepted.s: The principal environmental problem caused by aquaculture encroachment in Kolleru Lake is that it:
o: Eliminates all agricultural activity in the surrounding deltas
Turns the lake bed into ponds and fields, causing shrinkage and eutrophication
Converts freshwater into saline water through tidal action
Increases the lake’s depth and improves water circulation
accepted.x: Aquaculture ponds and fields have occupied portions of the lake bed, causing the lake to shrink and become eutrophic.
accepted.tq: Apply the cause-and-effect chain from land-use change to ecological impact.
accepted.sec: Kolleru lake aquaculture - encroachment issue

accepted.s: Water from which project’s right canal is planned to reach the Kolleru region?
accepted.x: Water from the Polavaram right canal is planned to reach the Kolleru region.
accepted.tq: Match the infrastructure project with its planned regional linkage.
accepted.sec: Kolleru lake aquaculture - encroachment issue
